# internal/retrieval/eval/testdata — fixture provenance (Art.2 §2)

## corpus.jsonl (6 documents)

Real files copied verbatim from `acamarata/cascade-v1` (archived, read-only
per `.claude/planning/p1/ARCHIVE-MAP.md`), harvested from the local archive
clone `../cascade-v1/` on 2026-09-06:

`docs/FABLE-FULL-REVIEW-PROMPT.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-P8-001-no-go-migration.md`,
`docs/cc-compat-matrix.md`, `docs/conductor-flow-contract.md`,
`docs/storage-estate.md`, `docs/target-dir-hygiene.md`.

Input only, per SPEC-SALVAGE: no v1 logic is reused, only the real document
text these six ids identify.

## known-item-queries.jsonl (18 queries)

Harvested verbatim from v1's own known-item ground truth,
`crates/cascade-rag/tests/fixtures/eval/queries.jsonl` (dataset
`cascade-docs-known-item` v1.0.0, generated by v1's own
`scripts/gen-eval-corpus.py` from commit `6c7ec3e35b0f994d0a488b2c35a678fbe59f4c42`),
restricted to the three queries whose `relevant_chunk_ids` is one of the six
documents above. Each query is a distinctive passage lifted out of its
source document by that script, so the ground truth is objective by
construction (the same method `internal/retrieval/testdata/README.md`'s
`fts5_queries.json` already establishes for this repo). Harvested from the
local archive clone on 2026-09-06.

## semantic-paraphrase-queries.jsonl (6 queries)

Hand-authored by this ticket, one per corpus document: each rephrases the
document's real topic in different words than the document's own text uses,
so a lexical (FTS5) match is weaker than it is for the known-item set while
the document is still the correct answer. This is deliberately NOT
machine-generated and NOT harvested — a semantic/paraphrase set has no
"real counterpart" to harvest the way a corpus document or a known-item
excerpt does; its provenance is that it was authored against the real
corpus documents above, by inspection, on 2026-09-06.

## recorded/real-embedder.jsonl

**This fixture does NOT come from a trained embedding model, and that gap
is the ticket's one unresolved contradiction with R-16.9 — recorded here
rather than hidden.** As of this ticket, the P1 tree has exactly one
`provider.Embedder` implementation anywhere in the module:
`providers/embeddings/bgem3`, whose own package doc states plainly "nothing
registers this client as an active embedder lane in P1; the sidecar it
speaks to is a separate post-P1 artifact." There is no other real embedder
— networked or local — reachable from this repository or this build
environment (no model weights, no sidecar process, no network access in
the unit lane per Art.7). R-16.9 requires "a fixture recorded from a real
embedder"; that literal requirement cannot be honestly satisfied today
without either (a) fabricating a plausible-sounding tool name for output
that was not actually produced by it, which Art.1 forbids more strongly
than shipping an honest gap, or (b) standing up the post-P1 sidecar
artifact, which is out of this ticket's scope and depends on work that has
not landed.

What is recorded instead: a deterministic term-count vectorizer
(`eval-harness-hashed-bow`, an internal one-off generation script, not
shipped code) over a curated 62-term vocabulary drawn from the six corpus
documents' real subject matter, applied to every document, known-item
query, and semantic/paraphrase query text used by this ticket's fixtures.
It is a real, describable, deterministic algorithm — not a mock that
ignores its input — but it is NOT a trained embedding model, and no claim
in this package or its docs states otherwise. `tool` in the fixture's JSON
says exactly this. Because the algorithm is lexical (word counts), it
shares FTS5's blind spot for paraphrases that reuse few of a document's
own words, so `FusionDefaultGate` measuring FAIL over
`semantic-paraphrase-queries.jsonl` is an expected, honest outcome of this
fixture's real limits, not a defect in the gate logic — see the ticket
journal for the measured verdict.

Loader note: despite the `.jsonl` extension (required verbatim by this
ticket's `files_scope`), the file is one JSON document, not
line-delimited — the Art.2 provenance fields (`tool`/`version`/`date`) sit
once alongside every recorded vector rather than repeating per line.

## v1-goldens/august-2026-baseline.json

Harvested verbatim from v1's own `crates/cascade-rag/tests/fixtures/eval/baseline.json`
(tool: `cascade-v1` `tests/retrieval_eval.rs`; version:
`archive/p9-integration` @ `539280154437c624fe816f7284925b22b68a12c1`; date:
2026-08-28, the file's real last-commit date in the archive clone).

**Second unresolved contradiction, quoted both ways:** the ticket contract
asks for "known-item, semantic/paraphrase, FTS5-only, and fused recall@10"
values to regress-check. v1's real fixture never measured any of that
shape: it reports MRR@10 (not recall@10), over its own 89-document/258-query
corpus (not this ticket's 6-document subset), computed with v1's
`MockEmbedModel::new(1024)` standing in for the vector leg (`tests/retrieval_eval.rs`
line ~97) — not a real embedder either. Relabeling `rrf_full`/`fts5_only`
as this ticket's recall@10 fields would misrepresent both the metric and
the embedder that produced them. What DOES transfer honestly across the
metric/corpus difference is the *ratio* `rrf_full / fts5_only` (how much of
FTS5-only's known-item quality the RRF leg retained): v1's own real,
harvested measurement already shows that ratio below 1
(`0.99160206 / 0.99418604 ≈ 0.99740`), and `TestV1August2026Baseline`
refuses a regression of that ratio on this ticket's own corpus — the one
comparison that stays meaningful when the absolute scale is not.
